picks.title: Fast, reliable A2UI, with swappable inference formats
picks.excerpt: Google's A2UI generative-UI protocol gets swappable inference formats, including A2UI Express for 3x lower latency and controlled generation with Jev for reliable agent-generated interfaces. (Off-list: no on-list outlet covered generative UI this window.)
picks.rationale: A primary-source release that adds A2UI Express, which Google says cuts latency 3x, plus controlled generation for agent-rendered UI. It matters to designers specifying generative interfaces. This is a protocol update, not the 10-12 'AI-generated UI' essay. It is the second workflow pick, so it gets the palette accent #3b6bff.

picks.title: Explore Shaders and Motion with the Figma agent | Figma on Figma
picks.excerpt: Figma's own team demos using the Figma agent to create shaders and motion on the canvas in an everyday workflow.
picks.rationale: Figma's team demonstrates the Figma agent producing shaders and motion on the canvas, a hands-on technique Figma users can copy. Earlier Figma-agent posts covered product-design craft (10-07) and design systems (10-24), not shaders or motion.

picks.title: Etsy's crackdown on AI slop is welcome, but it shows how far things have slipped
picks.excerpt: Etsy introduces a rule banning fake AI-generated product photos; Creative Bloq argues a handmade-design marketplace needing such a rule shows how far AI imagery has eroded trust.
picks.rationale: Etsy has a new rule banning fake AI-generated product photos. It directly affects designers and makers who sell there and shoot their own product images. This policy has not been covered before. The nearest earlier item is the 10-22 Just Eat AI menu-photo story, which is a different company and a different event.

picks.title: New CG software you may have missed: 25 October 2026 (EdenLive real-time AI renderer, KeenFace)
picks.excerpt: Round-up includes EdenLive, an open-source model that turns rough blockout animation into near-photorealistic video in real time on one consumer GPU, plus KeenFace AI 3D head generation and an MCP server in Gaffer.
picks.rationale: This week's round-up leads with releases not covered before: EdenLive, an open-source real-time blockout-to-photoreal renderer that runs on one consumer GPU, plus KeenFace AI head generation and a Gaffer MCP server. 3D and visualisation designers can try these now. It is a different instalment with different releases from the 18 October round-up published 10-20.

picks.title: CLI-Anything: Turn Any App Into a CLI for Claude Code and Codex
picks.excerpt: CLI-Anything auto-generates command-line interfaces for GIMP, Blender, LibreOffice and more, giving AI coding agents direct access to creative tools.
picks.rationale: CLI-Anything generates command-line interfaces for creative apps such as GIMP and Blender, so Claude Code or Codex can drive them directly. Designers get a practical way to script creative tools with agents. This is a different tool from the 10-08 logo skill-package item, which was SVG checks for agents.

The Verge Pages/Keynote/Numbers piece was excluded as well: it is the same Apple update, and gadgets ran it on 10-24. Replacements: the CG Channel 25 Oct round-up, a new weekly instalment whose releases (EdenLive, KeenFace, Gaffer MCP) differ from the 18 Oct round-up published 10-20, and MindStudio CLI-Anything, a new tool. Still excluded: The Verge Genie 4, because the games section picked the DeepMind Genie 4 primary source today (cross-section clash). MindStudio FLUX 3 Klein is the same story as the 10-16 Hugging Face post. DEV 'approval UX' duplicates the 10-11 DEV piece. NVIDIA RTX Spark continues the 10-14 story and belongs to games. Not picked for relevance: StandardFlow (engineering compliance), the Notion billboard (marketing), the Opus-vs-GPT 3D shoot-out, the DEV error-states and UX Collective essays (evergreen), the Config India keynote and the Adobe Stock short (promo).
